title: Trump merchandise and the T1 phone
summary: Every product named exists and pays Trump royalties: NFTs (Dec 2022), watches, gold sneakers, the God Bless the USA Bible, Victory 47 fragrances and the Trump Mobile T1. The T1 site did drop its 'Made in the USA' banner in late June 2025. Customers' details were exposed in a May 2026 Trump Mobile pre-order data leak. 'The family sells' glosses over the fact that these are mostly licensing deals run by third parties, and 'doxxed' describes a site vulnerability, not a targeted act.

sub_claims.statement: The Trump family has an NFT business.
sub_claims.finding: Trump Digital Trading Cards ($99) launched 15 Dec 2022, sold about 44-45k for about $4.45M, and were licensed via NFT INT LLC. The 2025 OGE disclosure listed about $1.16M in NFT licensing income.
Trump-branded watches launched Sept 2024, with some models up to $100,000. The disclosure reported $2.8M in Trump Watches royalties.
Gold 'Never Surrender' high-tops ($399) were unveiled at Sneaker Con in Feb 2024, licensed via CIC Ventures. Sneakers plus fragrances earned about $2.5M of 2024 income.
The 'God Bless the USA Bible' ($59.99, Mar 2024) paid $1,306,035 in royalties via Greenwood according to the 2025 disclosure.
'Victory 47' cologne and perfume ($99) went on sale in late 2024.

sub_claims.statement: The T1 phone was said to be made in America until the website was changed.
sub_claims.finding: Trump Mobile launched 16 June 2025: a $499 T1 and a $47.45/month plan, announced by Don Jr. and Eric Trump. The 'MADE IN THE USA' banner was replaced around 25-26 June 2025 by 'designed with American values in mind' / 'American-proud design'. The spokesperson insisted the phones are made in America. Shipping began May 2026 with units described as 'assembled in the U.S.' Warren-led Democrats asked the FTC to investigate in Aug 2025 and Jan 2026.

sub_claims.statement: Customers' details were exposed in a May 2026 leak of Trump Mobile pre-order data, described by one buyer as being 'doxxed'.
sub_claims.finding: In May 2026 a researcher found a flaw exposing Trump Mobile pre-order customers' names, emails, addresses, phone numbers and order IDs. One buyer said his own address and email were in the data. Trump Mobile confirmed the exposure, blamed a third-party platform and patched it. This was a mass data exposure, not targeted doxxing.

corrections: Claimed: the family sells these goods directly. The record shows: most are licensing deals (CIC Ventures, NFT INT LLC, Trump Mobile's operators) that pay royalties to Trump, and Trump Mobile's site disclaims Trump Organization manufacture or sale.
'Doxxed' is a loose word: customers' data was exposed in a site-wide pre-order vulnerability (May 2026), not published by anyone targeting an individual buyer.
The company never fully dropped the U.S. claim. It later said the first T1 units are 'assembled in the U.S.', which has not been independently verified.
denials_and_context: Trump Mobile spokesperson Chris Walker (June 2025): 'T1 phones are proudly being made in America. Speculation to the contrary is simply inaccurate.'
Trump Mobile confirmed the data exposure, attributed it to a third-party platform, and said it was evaluating whether to notify customers.
One buyer's analysis of the leaked data put real pre-orders at about 30,000 (some outlets say 10,000), against roughly 590,000 claimed earlier; this is that buyer's own inference from the leaked IDs.
These consumer products arguably matter less than the regulated industries the family is entering.

changes: No factual changes. Fresh coverage (Gizmodo, IBTimes, Fierce Network, Android Authority) matches. Added a lead: one buyer who analysed the leaked data said the exposed database showed about 10,000 unique customers and about 30,000 orders, against the roughly 590,000 pre-orders Trump Mobile claimed. Gizmodo could not independently verify the numbers. The claim that the T1 is a rebadged Chinese-made handset circulates online but is unverified.

leads.title: Trump Mobile's 590,000 pre-order claim vs. leaked order data
leads.why_connected: The May 2026 data exposure reportedly showed, according to one buyer's analysis of the leaked data, about 10,000 unique customers and about 30,000 orders, a fraction of the ~590,000 pre-orders Trump Mobile claimed. This bears on the venture's marketing claims, which Democrats have already asked the FTC to probe.
